en: The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Perception of Pleasure, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Yuezhi during the Western Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
In the Jeta Grove, at that time, the Blessed One addressed the bhikṣus:
"Regarding those śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas who perceive earth as earth, who delight in earth, and who reckon earth as 'I,' they say: 'Earth is my self.'"

I say that they do not yet know water, fire, wind, the devas, Brahmā, Ābhāsvara devas, and Avṛha devas; they perceive purity in what is pure, delight in purity, and reckon purity as self, saying, "Purity is my self.
I say that they do not yet know the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

Whether one or many, whether through individual seeing, hearing, cognition, or attainment, whether in this life or the next life, or from the next life to this life— if they possess such perceptions and attachments, and if they delight in these, regarding them as "this is mine" or "this is I," and if they reckon all of that to be "I," I say that they do not yet know.

Whosoever among śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas regards earth as a supernatural power (abhijñā), yet does not delight in earth, does not delight in earth, and does not regard earth as "I"—he does not say, "Earth is mine.
I declare that such a person has already understood water, fire, and wind.
The devas, the Brahmās, the Ābhāsvaras, and the Avṛhas take purity as their supernormal power, yet they do not delight in purity, do not delight in purity, and do not regard purity as "I.
I say that they have already realized the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

Whether one or many, whether hearing individually or through the consciousness of what is seen and heard, from this life to future lives, or from future lives to this life—they all, by means of supernormal powers, demonstrate neither delight nor non-delight, neither conceiving of a self, nor saying "this is me";
I say that they know this.

Furthermore, I take earth as my supernormal power (ṛddhi), yet I do not delight in earth; I do not delight in earth, nor do I take earth as a self, nor do I conceive of earth as "mine. I likewise know water, fire, and wind.

The gods of the Śuddhāvāsa, the Brahmakāyika, the Ābhāsvara, and the Avṛha—he does not regard their supernormal powers as pure; not regarding them as pure, he does not conceive of purity as "I. Through this, I know the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

Whether one or many, whether seen, heard, cognized, attained, observed, felt, or practiced—from this world to the next world, or from the next world to this world—having exhausted all supernormal powers, he does not delight in them; not delighting, he does not reckon them as "I";
"I have known this."
Thus the Buddha spoke.
Having heard what the World-Honored One had said, those bhikṣus rejoiced and were delighted; the section on causes was thus completed.
This concludes the *Sukhasaññā-sūtra* spoken by the Buddha.
